answer: On an island, agents surveying ferrous deposits near a summit could earn access to jobs through customer-issued work vouchers. Each paid, independently audited survey creates one voucher with a fixed total weight; transferring or splitting it across aliases preserves that weight. A Sybil swarm therefore needs additional useful surveys and paying customers to expand influence, incurring fieldwork and audit costs. Colluding customers can still buy fake work, and scarce vouchers may exclude newcomers. Sample raw measurements, cap voucher growth, and offer a small audited entry route.
